title: On the Use of Design-Based Simulations
abstract: arXiv:2603.11381v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Design-based simulations hold outcomes fixed and generate variation by resampling treatment assignment or shocks. They can be used in both methodological and applied work to assess inference procedures. However, their informativeness for these uses is not straightforward. We show that, when treatment effects are nonzero, these simulations can be misleading about spatial or serial correlation in clustered experiments, difference-in-differences, and shift-share designs. We analyze alternatives and formalize how these simulations can reveal features of the error distribution despite holding outcomes fixed. Finally, we consider limitations in the use of design-based simulations to select among different inference methods in applied work.

translated_title: 关于基于设计的模拟方法的使用
translated_abstract: 基于设计的模拟将结果保持固定，并通过重新抽样处理分配或冲击来产生变异。它们可以在方法论研究和应用研究中用于评估推断程序。然而，它们在这些用途中的信息价值并不直观。我们证明，当处理效应非零时，这些模拟在聚类实验、双重差分和移动份额设计中关于空间或序列相关性方面可能产生误导。我们分析了替代方法，并形式化了这些模拟如何在保持结果固定的同时揭示误差分布的特征。最后，我们考虑了在应用研究中使用基于设计的模拟来在不同推断方法之间进行选择时的局限性。
tldr: 该论文揭示了基于设计的模拟在处理效应非零时可能对聚类实验、双重差分和移动份额设计中的空间或序列相关性产生误导，并形式化了这些模拟揭示误差分布特征的条件及其在推断方法选择中的局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that design-based simulations can be misleading about spatial or serial correlation in clustered experiments, difference-in-differences, and shift-share designs when treatment effects are nonzero, and formalizes how these simulations can reveal features of the error distribution despite holding outcomes fixed, while also considering their limitations for selecting among different inference methods in applied work.
